chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn, from Zayd, from Ali, from al-Husayn, from his father, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Beautify your names, for you will be called by them on the Day of Resurrection: 'Arise, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, to your light,' and 'Arise, O So-and-so son of So-and-so, there is no light for you.'

key_terms.فُلَان: So-and-so (a placeholder name used in examples)

ai.seo_question: Why should Muslims choose good names according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the eschatological weight of naming in Shia tradition, where one's name serves as a spiritual identifier on the Day of Judgment, directly linking linguistic identity to divine light (nur). The Prophet’s instruction to 'beautify' names reflects the belief that a name is not merely a label but a reflection of the soul's inherent quality, with the call to 'light' signifying proximity to God and the absence of light indicating spiritual deficiency. This concept is deeply rooted in the Shia understanding of the names of the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful as vessels of divine illumination.
